title: Performance Profiling
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of performance profiling using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates performance profiling.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Performance Profiling** as part of **Software Engineering, Security, and Performance**. Measure a reproducible workload before optimizing, and compare correctness plus CPU, memory, allocation, and target-specific costs. Use the subtopics—Measuring Before Optimizing, CPU and Memory Profiling, Benchmarking and Reproducible Results—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with measuring before optimizing. Then compare it with cpu and memory profiling. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Measuring Before Optimizing
items.text: Measuring Before Optimizing is one part of performance profiling. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: CPU and Memory Profiling
items.text: CPU and Memory Profiling should be evaluated against input size, allocation behavior, and workload. Start with a correctness test and reproducible measurement; choose the simplest implementation that meets the requirement.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Run in the project that declares the necessary JVM, coroutine, networking, database, or serialization dependencies. Never commit real secrets.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: A source-code change is an optimization even without measurements.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.

items.title: Explain
items.text: Describe the main rule of performance profiling in your own words.

items.title: Apply
items.text: Change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

items.title: Verify
items.text: Check one edge case and the official reference for the selected Kotlin/runtime version.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small variation that demonstrates performance profiling. Write down your predicted result first, run it in the correct local project, then explain one boundary case involving measuring before optimizing.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain performance profiling without copying the lesson wording.
Demonstrate the concept with a small code/configuration change and state the expected result.
Test one boundary case or explain a relevant platform/version limitation.
hints: Begin with the first syllabus subtopic: Measuring Before Optimizing. What input or state does it act on?
Change only one value, branch, declaration, or dependency at a time. Predict what should happen before running the code.
Compare your observed result with the expected output and the official reference; verify that you are using the required project type and dependency set.
